items.title: KL is invariant under a measurable bijection
items.statement:
Let $\phi:(E,\mathcal E)\to(F,\mathcal F)$ be a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. For probability measures P,Q on E, let $\phi_\#P,\phi_\#Q$ be their push-forwards. Then
$$D(\phi_\#P\|\phi_\#Q)=D(P\|Q).$$
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited through the Radon–Nikodym definition of general KL.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.2
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.1

items.title: The product of two probability kernels is a probability kernel
items.statement: Let $(Z,\mathcal Z)$, $(E,\mathcal E)$, and $(F,\mathcal F)$ be measurable spaces, and let $K:Z\rightsquigarrow E$ and $L:Z\rightsquigarrow F$ be probability kernels. For each $z$, let $\Pi_z=K(z,\cdot)\otimes L(z,\cdot)$ be the finite product probability on $(E\times F,\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)$. Then $z\mapsto\Pi_z$ is a probability kernel.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used: each finite product probability is uniquely determined by its rectangle values.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.2 and 2.6
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3

items.title: Measure-theoretic mutual information
items.statement:
Let $(E,\mathcal E)$ and $(F,\mathcal F)$ be measurable spaces and let $P$ be a probability measure on $(E\times F,\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)$. Its marginals are $P_E(A)=P(A\times F)$ and $P_F(B)=P(E\times B)$. The product probability $P_E\otimes P_F$ exists by the finite product-measure theorem. Define the **measure-theoretic mutual information** of the joint law $P$ by
$$I(P):=D(P\|P_E\otimes P_F)\in[0,+\infty].$$
For random elements $X,Y$ with joint law $P_{XY}$, write $I(X;Y):=I(P_{XY})$. The logarithm convention is the natural logarithm, so finite values are in nats as fixed by [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The divergence is directional in its two law arguments and is $+\infty$ when $P_{XY}\not\ll P_X\otimes P_Y$.

This definition uses only the joint law, not a choice of density or a difference of entropy quantities.
items.strategy: Define the law functional directly through directional measurable-space KL and the product of the two marginals; keep the value extended nonnegative and do not express it as a difference of entropies.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the measurable-space KL definition through its Radon–Nikodym density; no additional choice is used.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.2–5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.4
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: The same-marginal conditional-product law is well-defined
items.statement:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces, and let $K(z,\cdot)$ and $L(z,\cdot)$ be supplied conditional laws of $X$ and $Y$ given $Z=z$. The product kernels $M(z,\cdot)=K(z,\cdot)\otimes L(z,\cdot)$ form a probability kernel. The joint law
$$R(C\times A\times B)=\int_C K(z,A)L(z,B)\,P_Z(dz)$$
exists uniquely on the product sigma-algebra and does not depend on the chosen versions of $K,L$. It has $Z$ marginal $P_Z$ and conditional law $M$ for $(X,Y)$ given $Z$.
items.axiom_base: AC supplies standard-Borel conditional-law existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness. Finite product kernels and joint laws use no additional choice.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.3 and 5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.4 and 2.6

items.title: Variational and finite-partition formulas for measurable-space KL
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space. For bounded measurable real $f$, put
$$\Phi_{P,Q}(f):=\int f\,dP-\ln\int e^f\,dQ.$$
Then
$$D(P\|Q)=\sup_{f\ {\rm bounded\ measurable}}\Phi_{P,Q}(f).$$
Equivalently, for every finite measurable partition $\mathcal P=(A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ of the whole space,
$$D(P\|Q)=\sup_{\mathcal P}\sum_{i=1}^m P(A_i)\ln\frac{P(A_i)}{Q(A_i)},$$
where $0\ln(0/q)=0$ and a term with $P(A_i)>0=Q(A_i)$ is $+\infty$. The result includes singular and infinite-divergence cases.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the Radon–Nikodym definition of general KL and its nonnegativity theorem.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.2, Theorem 5.2.1
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.4, Theorem 3.7
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 5 §5.1, Theorem 5.1.1

items.title: Finite-alphabet conditional entropy given an observation
items.statement:
Let $X$ take values in a finite nonempty set $S$ and let $Y$ take values in a standard-Borel space $(T,\mathcal T)$. Let $K:T\rightsquigarrow S$ be a conditional law of $X$ given $Y$, so that $K(Y,\cdot)$ is a regular conditional distribution given $\sigma(Y)$. Define
$$H(X\mid Y):=\int_T\left(-\sum_{x\in S}K(y,\{x\})\ln K(y,\{x\})\right)P_Y(dy),$$
with $0\ln0:=0$ and natural logarithms. The finite entropy convention is that of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Each evaluation $y\mapsto K(y,\{x\})$ is measurable. The explicit argument in [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]] proves $-t\ln t$ extends continuously to zero and is bounded by $1/e$ on $[0,1]$; hence the finite entropy integrand is measurable and bounded by $|S|/e$. The result is independent of the supplied version by simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness of standard-Borel regular conditional laws.

This definition permits a non-finite observation Y; only the target alphabet S is finite. If Y is finite, then for each positive-mass y the conditional-law identity gives $K(y,\{x\})P_Y(\{y\})=P(X=x,Y=y)$, so $K(y,\{x\})=p_{X|y}(x)$. Evaluating the integral as a finite weighted sum therefore gives exactly the convention of [[def-it-finite-conditional-entropy]], by [[cor-expectation-agrees-with-the-finite-weighted-sum]].
items.strategy: Average the bounded finite-alphabet entropy of a supplied regular conditional law; use standard-Borel disintegration and almost-everywhere uniqueness to justify the version convention.
items.axiom_base: AC supplies the regular conditional law of the finite-valued variable given the standard-Borel observation and the simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness used for version independence; it is also an explicit hypothesis of the cited general KL interface used for continuity and boundedness of t ln t.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Law entropy as self-mutual information
items.statement:
For a random element $X$ with law $P_X$, define its **law entropy** by
$$H(X):=I(X;X)=D(P_{XX}\|P_X\otimes P_X),$$
where $P_{XX}$ is the joint law of the diagonal pair $(X,X)$. This is an extended nonnegative quantity in nats and depends only on the law of X.
items.strategy: Use the general joint-KL definition on the diagonal joint law of (X,X); do not use differential-entropy subtraction.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited through the general measurable-space KL in the mutual-information definition.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Conditional mutual information by a same-marginal product law
items.statement:
Let X,Y,Z be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces and joint law $P_{XYZ}$. Let $K(z,\cdot)$ and $L(z,\cdot)$ be regular conditional laws of X and Y given Z=z. Let R be the probability law on the product space whose rectangle values are
$$R(C\times A\times B)=\int_C K(z,A)L(z,B)\,P_Z(dz).$$
Its existence, uniqueness, and independence of the versions K,L are established in [[lem-same-marginal-conditional-product-law-well-defined]]. Define the **conditional mutual information** by
$$I(X;Y\mid Z):=D(P_{XYZ}\|R)\in[0,+\infty].$$
The reference R has the same Z marginal as the joint law and makes X,Y independent conditionally on Z. The logarithm is natural, so finite values are measured in nats under [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The definition is a divergence between full probability laws; it does not subtract two possibly infinite entropies.
items.strategy: Use the uniquely defined joint law formed from the product of regular conditional marginals; its version independence makes the divergence a function of the joint law.
items.axiom_base: AC is required for regular conditional law existence and uniqueness on standard-Borel spaces and for the Radon–Nikodym KL definition.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5

items.title: Conditional KL is measurable for supplied kernels
items.statement: Let K,L be probability kernels from a measurable space $(Z,\mathcal Z)$ into a standard-Borel space $(E,\mathcal E)$. Then $z\mapsto D(K(z,\cdot)\|L(z,\cdot))$ is $\mathcal Z$-measurable, with $+\infty$ allowed. Consequently the integral used to define conditional KL is well-defined.
items.axiom_base: AC supplies the countable generating algebra for a standard-Borel target and the Radon–Nikodym KL definition.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.6
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3

items.title: Conditional KL for supplied probability kernels
items.statement:
Let $(Z,\mathcal Z)$ and $(E,\mathcal E)$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $Z$, and let $K,L:Z\rightsquigarrow E$ be supplied probability kernels. Define their **conditional KL divergence with base $\mu$** by
$$D_\mu(K\|L):=\int_Z D(K(z,\cdot)\|L(z,\cdot))\,\mu(dz)\in[0,+\infty].$$
The integrand is measurable by [[thm-conditional-kl-is-measurable]], so this is a well-defined nonnegative extended integral. No absolute-continuity assumption is imposed on individual fibers; a singular fiber has divergence $+\infty$. Changing supplied kernel versions on a $\mu$-null set does not change the integral.
items.strategy: Use a supplied pair of kernels and common base measure; justify measurability of the fiber divergence by the local variational representation theorem.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from measurable-space KL and the countable determining-algebra interface used for standard-Borel kernels.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.2 and 2.6

items.title: Law entropy and differential entropy are different quantities
items.statement:
For a probability law with Lebesgue density $f$ on $\mathbb R^d$, its **differential entropy**, when the integral is defined, is
$$h(f):=-\int_{\mathbb R^d} f(x)\ln f(x)\,dx.$$
This density-based quantity is not the law entropy $H(X)=I(X;X)$ of [[def-law-entropy-as-self-mutual-information]]. Differential entropy may be finite or negative even when law entropy is infinite; the uniform law on $[0,1]$ is a basic example. No identity between the two is used in this page.
items.strategy: State the two definitions and their distinct domains; use the uniform distribution example as the concrete contrast.

references.title: John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 1 and Chapter 5 §5.5

items.title: Finite-alphabet conditional entropy is version-invariant and obeys its chain rule
items.statement:
Let $X,U$ take values in finite nonempty sets and $Z$ in a standard-Borel space. Conditional entropy as defined in [[def-finite-alphabet-conditional-entropy-given-observation]] is unchanged when any supplied regular conditional law is replaced by another version. Moreover,
$$H(X,U\mid Z)=H(X\mid Z)+H(U\mid X,Z).$$
All three quantities are finite; the identity is an additive finite-sum identity.
items.axiom_base: AC is used for standard-Borel regular conditional law existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Self-mutual-information entropy on countable and non-atomic laws
items.statement:
Let X have a probability law P on a standard-Borel space. Let $S=\{x:P(\{x\})>0\}$ be its set of atoms. Then S is countable. If $P(S)=1$ and its atom masses are $(p_i)$, the law entropy from [[def-law-entropy-as-self-mutual-information]] is
$$H(X)=\sum_i p_i\ln\frac1{p_i},$$
with value $+\infty$ allowed. If $P(S)<1$, then $H(X)=+\infty$.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the measurable-space KL definition. Enumerating a countable set of atoms uses the stated standard set-theoretic choice base.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapters 1 and 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Zero information is exactly independence
items.statement: Let X,Y,Z be standard-Borel random elements. Then $I(X;Y)=0$ if and only if $P_{XY}=P_X\otimes P_Y$ (independence). Also $I(X;Y\mid Z)=0$ if and only if X and Y are conditionally independent given $\sigma(Z)$ in the sense of [[def-conditional-independence-given-a-sigma-algebra]].
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from general KL and regular-conditional-law existence; the conditional-independence class convention also assumes AC.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4, Theorem 2.5

items.title: Mutual information is recovered by finite coordinate quantizations
items.statement:
A **finite quantizer** on a measurable space is a measurable map into a finite set. Let X,Y,Z be standard-Borel random elements. Choose sequences of finite quantizers $q_n$ on X and $r_n$ on Y whose generated sigma-algebras increase to the full sigma-algebras of their respective spaces. Then
$$I(X;Y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}I(q_n(X);r_n(Y))$$
and
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)=\lim_{n\to\infty}I(q_n(X);r_n(Y)\mid Z).$$
Such sequences exist by countable generation of standard-Borel sigma-algebras. In the conditional formula, Z remains unchanged.
items.axiom_base: AC is used through the countable generating-algebra and standard-Borel conditional-law suppliers.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5, Lemmas 5.5.5 and 5.5.7
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.4

items.title: KL chain rule for standard-Borel disintegrations
items.statement:
Let $E,F$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $\mu,
u$ be probability measures on E, and let $K,L:Eightsquigarrow F$ be probability kernels. Let $P=\mu\ltimes K$ and $Q=
u\ltimes L$ be the joint probability laws defined by
$$P(C)=\int_E K(x,C_x)\,\mu(dx),\qquad Q(C)=\int_E L(x,C_x)\,
u(dx)$$
for product-measurable $C\subseteq E	imes F$. Then
$$D(P\|Q)=D(\mu\|
u)+\int_E D(K(x,\cdot)\|L(x,\cdot))\,\mu(dx)
=D(\mu\|
u)+D_\mu(K\|L),$$
as an equality in $[0,+\infty]$. In particular, when $\mu=
u$, the joint KL is the conditional KL from [[def-conditional-kl-for-probability-kernels]].
items.axiom_base: AC supplies the Radon–Nikodym densities and the countable determining algebra. Conditional kernels are supplied, not selected in the proof.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3, Lemmas 5.3.1–5.3.2 and Theorem 5.3.2
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.2

items.title: Mutual-information chain rule without subtracting infinities
items.statement:
For standard-Borel random elements X,Y,Z,
$$I((Z,X);Y)=I(Z;Y)+I(X;Y\mid Z).$$
The right side is a sum in $[0,+\infty]$. This chain rule is asserted as an equality of extended nonnegative quantities; no difference of possibly infinite entropies or divergences occurs.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from measurable-space KL and standard-Borel disintegration; all conditional laws in the proof are supplied by those interfaces.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.3 and 5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: A finite deterministic copy has mutual information equal to entropy
items.statement:
Let $X$ be Bernoulli with $P(X=1)=p$ and $P(X=0)=1-p$, and set $Y=X$. Then
$$I(X;Y)=H(X)=-p\ln p-(1-p)\ln(1-p),$$
where $H(X)$ means the finite Shannon entropy of the probability vector of X and $0\ln0=0$.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from measurable-space KL. The finite entropy and the identification of a finite discrete law use no additional choice.

items.title: Coarsening the conditioning variable can increase conditional mutual information
items.statement:
Let X be a fair bit and let $Y=X$. Set $Z=(X,Y)$ and let W be constant. Then
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)=0,\qquad I(X;Y\mid W)=\ln2.$$
Thus replacing Z by its coarsening W can increase conditional mutual information.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4

items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from standard-Borel conditional laws and measurable-space KL; all displayed finite sums are choice-free.

items.title: Changing a conditional kernel on a null fiber leaves information unchanged
items.statement: Let Z be uniform on the Borel unit interval and let X=Y=0 almost surely, with finite value space $\{0,1\}$. The regular conditional kernels $K(z)=L(z)=\delta_0$ may be replaced by $K'(0)=\delta_1$, $K'(z)=\delta_0$ for $z>0$, and $L'(z)=\delta_0$. The pointwise conditional KL between the conditional joint law of $(X,Y)$ and the product of these marginal kernels changes from zero everywhere to $+\infty$ at $z=0$, but its $P_Z$-integral and $I(X;Y\mid Z)$ remain zero.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.3 and 5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.4 and 2.6

items.axiom_base: Countable choice normalizes the uniform conditioning law; AC is inherited from measurable-space KL. The displayed kernels and their null-set modifications are constructed explicitly.

items.title: The uniform law has infinite self-information entropy and zero differential entropy
items.statement: Let $P$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to the Borel unit interval $[0,1]$, and let $X$ be the identity random element on that probability space. Its law entropy $H(X)=I(X;X)$ is $+\infty$, whereas its differential entropy is $0$.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapters 1 and 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.axiom_base: The box-volume supplier assumes countable choice; the self-information entropy theorem inherits AC through measurable-space KL.
